diagnostic_evidence.quote: We make use of the abbreviation $d_s := d_s(B_{\CC,\bsigma},L_2(U,\CC;\mu))$. In our setting, we know $d_s = \sigma_{s+1}^{-1}$.
Let $m := n$ and $\lceil 20 n\log n\rceil$ points be drawn i.i.d.\ with respect to $\nu$.

issues.failure_explanation: The least-squares algorithm $S_{cn}^X$ is a projection onto $V_m\otimes X$, so its worst-case error over the unit ball is at least the Kolmogorov width: $\sup_{v\in B_{X,\bsigma}}\|v-S_{cn}^Xv\|\ge d_m=\sigma_{m+1}^{-1}$. The stated bounds can be strictly smaller than $d_m$ (or $d_n$) for admissible spectra with a sharp eigenvalue drop. For (iii), take $\sigma_s^{-2}=1$ for $s\le n$ and $\sigma_s^{-2}=\epsilon 2^{n+1-s}$ for $s>n$ (non-decreasing $\bsigma$, $\bsigma^{-1}\in\ell_2$): then $\sqrt{\frac1n\sum_{s\ge n}d_s^2}=\sqrt{2\epsilon/n}<\sqrt\epsilon=d_n$ for $n>2$, while the error is $\ge d_n$. For (ii), a drop after $n+1$ gives $\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}(1+2\epsilon)}<1=d_n$ for large $n$. For (i), with $m=\lfloor n/(20\log n)\rfloor$ and a drop after $n/\log n$, $d_m=1$ but the bound is $\sqrt{2\epsilon\log n/n}<1$. Thus the cited bounds (KU21, BSU23, DKU23) are mis-stated or applied outside their valid hypotheses; a regularity condition on the spectrum is needed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the three bounds with valid ones of the correct order (e.g., $C d_m\sqrt{\log n}$ for (i) and (ii) and $C d_n$ for (iii), using the correct sampling-number estimates), or add an explicit regularity hypothesis on $\bsigma$; the rates $MN(n/\log n)^{-1/q}$, $MNn^{-1/q}\sqrt{\log n}$, $MNn^{-1/q}$ are then recovered via $d_m\le Nm^{-1/q}$ and $d_n\le Nn^{-1/q}$.
issues.overall_effect: The sharp algorithm-level bounds (i), (ii), (iii) are false for spectra with a sharp eigenvalue drop. The proofs of Theorem thm:varrho_n (i)--(iii), Theorem theorem:varrho_n><, Theorem theorem:sampling-lognormal-affine (i)--(iii), and Theorem theorem:sampling-lognormal-holomorphic (i)--(iii) all rely on these bounds, so those proofs are invalid as written. The advertised convergence rates $MN(n/\log n)^{-1/q}$, $MNn^{-1/q}\sqrt{\log n}$, and $MNn^{-1/q}$ remain valid (since $d_m\le Nm^{-1/q}$ and $d_n\le Nn^{-1/q}$), but they are not established by the given arguments.
issues.title: Stated least-squares error bounds in Theorem thm:leastsquaresbounds (i)--(iii) can fall below the Kolmogorov width, which lower-bounds the algorithm's error
issues.why_classification: The sharp bounds are false for admissible spectra, so a nontrivial correction of the core technical theorem is needed; however the advertised convergence rates and the regime survive through the Kolmogorov-width estimate $d_n\le Nn^{-1/q}$, so no rate materially worsens and no new global proof architecture is required.

issues.failure_explanation: The left side equals $M\sup_{v\in B_{X,\bsigma}}\|v-S_{cn}^Xv\|=M\|I-S_{cn}^X\|_{H_{X,\bsigma}\to L_2}$, whereas the right side as written equals $MN\|I-S_{cn}^X\|$ (when $B_{X,\bsigma}^q(1,1)$ is read as the unit ball), forcing $N=1$; moreover $B_{X,\bsigma}^q(1,1)$ is only defined under $\|\bsigma^{-1}\|_{\ell_q}\le1$, which is not assumed (only $\le N$ is). The $N$-dependence actually enters through the tail estimate $\sum_{s\ge m}\sigma_s^{-2}\le N^2m^{1-2/q}$, which the proof invokes only via the incomplete display \eqref{rho_n<} whose left-hand side is missing. Relatedly, the chain in item (iii), $\varrho_n \ll \sup_v\|v-S_{c_3n}^Xv\|$, is not the trivial relation (the trivial one is $\varrho_{c_3n}\le\sup_v\|v-S_{c_3n}^Xv\|$). The claims (i)--(iii) are nonetheless true via the correct scaling $M\sup_{v\in B_{X,\bsigma}}\|v-S_{cn}^Xv\|$ combined with the tail estimate.

failure_location.quote: \sup_{v\in B_{X,\bsigma}^{q}(M,N)} \norm{v - S_{cn}^X v}{L_2(U,X;\mu)} \ =\ MN \sup_{v\in B_{X,\bsigma}^{q}(1,1)} \norm{v - S_{cn}^X v}{L_2(U,X;\mu)}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false identity by $\sup_{v\in B_{X,\bsigma}^q(M,N)}\|v-S_{cn}^Xv\|=M\sup_{v\in B_{X,\bsigma}}\|v-S_{cn}^Xv\|$ and derive the $N$-dependence from the tail estimate $\sum_{s\ge m}\sigma_s^{-2}\le N^2m^{1-2/q}$; complete the display \eqref{rho_n<} and correct the index in the (iii) chain.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem thm:varrho_n is invalid as written, but the stated rates survive; the application theorems (theorem:sampling-lognormal-affine, theorem:sampling-lognormal-holomorphic) inherit the gap, though their conclusions remain valid.
issues.title: False scaling identity in the proof of Theorem thm:varrho_n
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of the scaling identity plus the standard tail estimate preserves every claim and rate in the theorem, with no new lemma, construction, or reoptimization needed.
